item.title: Long-Range Toric Code: Finite-Temperature Topological Order in Two Dimensions
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Jacopo Gliozzi, Taylor L. Hughes, Kyung-Su Kim
arXiv:2610.37765v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce two-dimensional toric code models with additional long-range loop interactions. Our models preserve the topologically ordered ground states of the ordinary toric code, while confining anyons at zero temperature. For sufficiently long-ranged interactions, we argue that this confinement persists at finite temperatures, strongly constraining anyon mobility and giving rise to finite-temperature topological order. This topological phase acts as a self-correcting quantum memory and exhibits long-range entanglement. For shorter-ranged interactions, signatures of topological order survive only up to an exponentially large length scale at finite temperature, yielding a partially self-correcting quantum memory.

item.title: Topological Quantum Error-Correcting Thresholds of a Symmetry-Enriched Toric Code
item.description:
📚 arXiv
👤 Jiasheng He, Ryan Thorngren
arXiv:2610.37791v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the error thresholds of a new topological quantum error-correcting code under the independent bit-flip and phase-flip noisy channel. By mapping to classical spin-glass models, we find that if Pauli X and Z errors are equally probable, the threshold of vertex syndromes is improved by 30% compared to that of the toric code, while the threshold of plaquette syndromes is lowered. Both thresholds increase when the Z component is less likely than the X component, reaching 0.5 if the Z component is absent. An analytical proof justifies this special case of perfect correctability, and a disordered version of Peierls's argument establishes a lower bound for the vertex-syndrome threshold.
